description: Between the end of the war of 1870 and August 1914, Europe believed in progress. Electricity, world's fairs, brand-new art movements, and the cracks that led to catastrophe.

hero.hook: Forty years of faith in progress, and then everything collapsed in 1914.

blocks.text: The **Belle Époque** was the stretch of relative peace between the end of the [[Franco-Prussian War]] (**1871**) and the outbreak of the [[First World War]] (**1914**). People believed in science, in progress, in reason.

For the well-off classes of Western Europe, these were four decades of comfort and invention. But under the varnish, social divisions and national rivalries were already burning, and they would blow everything apart.

A second industrial revolution brought **electricity**, **oil**, and chemistry. The tram and the subway (Paris, **1900**) reshaped the city. The car and the airplane were born. The telephone shrank distances.

blocks.caption: The 1900 World's Fair in Paris, a showcase for progress

blocks.text: The name “Belle Époque” only appeared after **1914**. The people who lived through it never thought they were living in a “Belle Époque.” The survivors of the trenches invented that lost paradise.

The **1900 World's Fair** drew **50 million** visitors. Cinema, invented by the Lumière brothers, and the Moulin Rouge made Paris a capital of entertainment. [[Auguste Comte's Positivism]], a very influential philosophy, summed up the mood: science would solve everything.
Behind the boulevards, workers often put in **10 to 12 hours** a day with no real protection. Urban poverty fed the tension between classes.

blocks.caption: The Eiffel Tower (1889), icon of a modernity that did not reach everyone

blocks.text: On the world stage, Europe carved up Africa. The [[Berlin Conference]] (**1884-1885**) drew borders without asking the peoples who lived inside them. In France, the [[Dreyfus Affair]] tore the Republic apart: Alfred Dreyfus, a Jewish officer, was wrongly convicted of spying, and anti-Semitism broke into the open.

The arts exploded. [[Art Nouveau]] curved the facades of buildings. [[Fauvism]] and [[Cubism]] shook up painting. The physician [[Sigmund Freud]] explored the unconscious. In **1905**, Albert Einstein published his theory of [[Relativity]]: space and time were no longer what people had assumed.
In **1913**, Igor Stravinsky's ballet *The Rite of Spring* caused such a scandal in Paris that members of the audience came to blows.

Then everything collapsed. On **28 June 1914**, Archduke **Franz Ferdinand**, heir to Austria-Hungary, was assassinated in Sarajevo. The machinery of alliances started turning. On **4 August**, the United Kingdom entered the war. Faith in progress died in the trenches.

events.detail: A unified Germany was born, along with lasting French resentment.
